plain.li: {X_nameDef} says out on the road they call us "the place that lets them go". I've been saying it under my breath all day. There are worse things to be called.
A traveler asked me if it's true we patch up raiders and send them home. I said yes. {X_nameDef} looked at me as if I'd said we feed wolves by hand.
[trait:Kind] {X_nameDef} slept well here because we spare our prisoners. Mercy as a reason to trust someone. I'll take that.
[afterraid] The fighting was two days ago and {X_nameDef} has already heard we tended the wounded ones. Word travels faster than the wounded do.
[old] I've lived long enough to see a lot of hard places. Being known as the soft one is new. I find I don't mind it.
[trait:Bloodlust|trait:Psychopath] {X_nameDef} called us merciful, to my face, as if it were a compliment. I smiled. It took some doing.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} thanked us for something we did for people {X_pronoun} never met. That's how you know a name has gone out ahead of you.

blunt.li: Apparently we're famous for not killing people. Low bar. Glad we clear it.

cheerful.li: They talk about us on the road! The kind things! {X_nameDef} said so!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} says we're known for mercy. Someday someone will come to test that. I hope we pass.

cold.li: {X_nameDef} trusts us because we're merciful. Useful. People who trust you tell you things.

plain.li: A visitor pulled a child back when I came near. I was going to wave. I kept my hand in my pocket the rest of the day.
{X_nameDef} says the people back home use our name to scare children indoors. I keep wondering which of us they mean.
[trait:Kind] I live in a colony people are afraid of. I don't know when that happened. I was here the whole time.
[night] Couldn't sleep. Kept seeing the way {X_nameDef} looked at me, as if I might do something.
[afterraid] After what we did to the last raiders, I suppose the stories are fair. I just didn't expect to hear them over supper.
[trait:Bloodlust] The visitors went quiet whenever I walked by. Best day in weeks.

warm.li: {X_nameDef}'s child smiled at me before being pulled away. One of them, at least, hasn't heard the stories yet.

blunt.li: They're scared of us. Fine. Scared people don't raid.

gloomy.li: We have a name on the road now. It's not one I'd have picked.

cold.li: {X_nameDef} watched my hands the whole visit. Good instincts.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} walked a day out of {X_possessive} way to eat at our table, on the strength of a rumor. The rumor was right. I made sure of it.
Fed a traveler today. {X_nameDef} ate like {X_pronoun} hadn't in a week, and maybe hadn't.
[winter] A bowl of stew in winter, for a stranger. It's not much. Out there it's everything.
[trait:Greedy] Another stranger at the kitchen door. They come because they know we'll give. That's the trouble with being known for something.
[poor] We don't have much. We gave {X_nameDef} some of it anyway. That's the whole idea, I think.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} said {X_pronoun} would tell everyone about our bread. I hope {X_pronoun} tells them about the stew too. The stew is better.

blunt.li: Fed {X_nameDef}. Didn't ask for anything. That's the deal here, apparently.

cheerful.li: {X_nameDef} had seconds AND thirds! I'm counting that as a review!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} ate everything I gave {X_objective} and looked at the pot for more. I gave more. Winter will remember.

cold.li: A bowl of stew buys more goodwill than a cartload of silver. Cheapest trade we make.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} brought {X_possessive} own bread to our table because {X_pronoun} heard we wouldn't share. I shared. On purpose. Loudly.
We have a name on the road for counting every grain. I counted mine, and gave {X_nameDef} some anyway.
[trait:Kind] A guest thought we'd charge for water. I don't want to be the kind of place people think that about.
Somebody out there is telling people we're misers. I'd like to know who. I'd like to give them something, out of spite.
[rich] We've got full storerooms and a name for stinginess. Both can't be right forever.

warm.li: I gave {X_nameDef} the good stew and wouldn't take a coin. {X_nameDef} looked surprised. Good. Let {X_objective} be surprised all the way home.

blunt.li: {X_nameDef} offered to pay for a cup of water. A cup of water. I'm still annoyed.

cheerful.li: Showed {X_nameDef} we're not stingy at all! Gave {X_objective} everything! Well. Some things.

gloomy.li: Maybe we have become misers. Maybe I only noticed today.

cold.li: A stranger thinks we're tight-fisted. Fine. It keeps the beggars off. I gave {X_objective} a cup anyway, since a cup costs nothing.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} watched us bless the bread and went quiet. Said {X_possessive} mother used to do that. Some things are worth keeping just so somebody can remember.
An old traveler sang our evening song with us. Wrong words in the second verse. Right in every way that counts.
[old] {X_nameDef} said we keep the old ways better than the towns do. I've been saying that for years. Nice to have a witness.
[teen] A traveler got misty over the way we say grace. It's just grace. Isn't it?
[evening] We sang the old song at supper and a stranger knew it. For a minute nobody was a stranger.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} thanked us for keeping the old customs, as if we were keeping them for {X_objective}. Maybe we are.

blunt.li: {X_nameDef} praised our customs. Good. Somebody should.

cheerful.li: A real old traveler knew our song! We're keeping something alive here!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} said nobody does the old things anymore, except us. It's a lonely sort of compliment.

cold.li: Visitors trust old customs. {X_nameDef} trusted us within the hour.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} came all this way to see what we're trying. I showed {X_objective} everything. I didn't know I was this proud of the drying racks.
Somebody on the road has been telling people we're the place where new things happen. I'd like to thank them.
[teen] A traveler wanted to see our new ideas! I gave the tour and made some of it up as I went, which is very much the spirit of the place.
[old] A visitor wanted to see all our new things. I showed {X_objective} around, then went and sat by the old well, which hasn't moved yet.
[skill:Crafting|skill:Construction] {X_nameDef} asked how we built the new oven. I explained. {X_nameDef} wrote it down. Somebody wrote down my idea.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} might take some of our ideas home. Good. Ideas are for sharing.

blunt.li: {X_nameDef} asked why we change everything. Because the old way was worse. Next question.

cheerful.li: {X_nameDef} said our furrows were MAD. In a good way! I think!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} admired everything we're trying. Half of it won't work. I didn't mention that.

cold.li: Visitors come to look at our experiments. Fine. I watch which ones they look at longest.

plain.li: The visitors took their boots off tonight. That's how you know a place is safe: boots off, songs on.
{X_nameDef} told me all the news from the road and taught me a song I won't get out of my head for a week.
[night] {X_nameDef} fell asleep by the fire in the middle of a story. I finished it for the others. I think I told it better.
[large] So many voices at the fire tonight, ours and theirs, that I couldn't tell where the colony stopped.
[trait:Abrasive] The visitors sang until midnight. Every one of them. Every verse.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} said this is the friendliest place on the road. I'm writing that down so I remember it in winter.

blunt.li: Guests stayed up late singing. Fine. They can sing while they chop wood next time.

cheerful.li: Songs! News! {X_nameDef} knows one about a miller with the worst luck in the world! Best night all season!

gloomy.li: Everyone was happy at the fire tonight. I kept wondering which of the visitors we'll never see again.

cold.li: Relaxed guests talk. {X_nameDef} told me more in one evening than a trader would in a year.

plain.li: The visitors kept their hands where we could see them all day. {X_nameDef} even asked before walking to the well. I don't know if I'm proud or ashamed.
{X_nameDef} asked where guests are allowed to stand. I knew the answer. That bothered me more than the question.
[trait:Kind] A guest asked my leave to sit down. In our yard. Is that who we are now?
[trait:Abrasive] Visitors who don't touch anything and leave on time. Perfect guests. More places should be like ours.
[afterraid] After the last raid, nobody gets past the gate without being looked over. {X_nameDef} understood. Didn't make it pleasant for either of us.

warm.li: I brought {X_nameDef} a cup of something warm, since {X_pronoun} wasn't to come further in. {X_nameDef} looked surprised. Somehow that made it worse.

blunt.li: Strangers stay where we put them. That's the rule. It's a good rule.

cheerful.li: The visitors were SO polite today. A bit scared, maybe. But so polite!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} wasn't afraid of what we'd do. {X_nameDef} was afraid of what we'd think {X_pronoun} was going to do.

cold.li: {X_nameDef} kept {X_possessive} hands visible the whole visit. Sensible.

plain.li: A trader stood at the edge of the fields and said, "Not a weed." Three words. I've been carrying them around all day.
{X_nameDef} said we're known for working dark to dark. I was going to argue, but I'd been up since before dawn.
[trait:Industrious|trait:HardWorker] {X_nameDef} counted our woodpile twice. I only counted it once, but I stacked it.
[trait:Lazy|trait:Slothful] A trader admired how hard we all work. I nodded along from the shade.
[skill:Plants] {X_nameDef} admired the rows. I planted those rows. I wanted to say so. I didn't. I'm saying it here.

warm.li: {X_nameDef} said our fields would shame a monastery. I'll tell the others at supper, when they're too tired to argue.

blunt.li: Trader liked the fields. Of course {X_pronoun} did. We work.

cheerful.li: A trader said our fields are the tidiest {X_pronoun} has EVER seen! Not a weed!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} admired our work. Didn't see our hands, though.

cold.li: Our fields impress traders. Impressed traders pay better.

plain.li: {X_nameDef} watched us nap at midday and asked if we needed anyone else. Where {X_nameDef} comes from, naps get you beaten.
A traveler envies how we live. Long lunches, no bells, no one counting. I'd never thought of it as something to envy.
[trait:Industrious|trait:HardWorker] A traveler envies our slow pace. I don't. I'm the reason it isn't slower.
[trait:Lazy|trait:Slothful] A stranger envies us. Of course. We've got it worked out here.
[summer] Shade, a cup of something, and a stranger telling me I've got the best life on the road. Could be worse.

warm.li: I told {X_nameDef} {X_pronoun} could stay a while and rest. {X_nameDef} looked as if nobody had said that to {X_objective} in years.

blunt.li: {X_nameDef} wrote down when we eat breakfast. When everyone's up. It's not complicated.

cheerful.li: A traveler wants to LIVE here because of our lunches! Our lunches are excellent!

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} envies how slow we are. I hope nothing ever comes fast enough to catch us.

cold.li: Travelers think we're soft because we rest. Let them think that.
